title: Priority fallback router and transparent retry slimming for hosted API streaming timeouts
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Summary:
During a customer escalation on 2026-03-09 we observed multi-tenant streaming sessions entering long-tail timeouts where client SDK retries and proxy fanout amplified latency, producing sustained 5xx responses for affected tenants. This ticket implements a short-lived, low-risk mitigation (priority fallback router + transparent retry slimming) and a follow-up hard fix path to eliminate amplification sources.

Observed behavior:
- Long tail streaming timeouts surfaced primarily for multi-chunk responses and resumable sessions.
- Clients retried aggressively after intermittent chunk timeouts; edge proxies and the serving runtime accepted retries and replayed requests to fragile backend pools.
- Retry amplification caused KV cache churn and inflight memory pressure on GPU nodes which led to 503/504 responses and elevated p50/p95 latency.

Root cause hypothesis (constructed from traces and profiling):
1) Edge admitted retries without tenant-aware admission limits; transient slow chunks triggered full replays.
2) Serving runtime's streaming deserialization path held buffers longer under retries; combined with KV cache eviction warmed by retries produced memory stalls.
3) Lack of per-tenant retry-hysteresis let clients escalate retries concurrently, creating admission storms.

Immediate mitigation implemented (this ticket's scope):
- Implement a Priority Fallback Router: for requests tagged as "streaming-resume" or with resumable tokens, route to a trimmed execution path with stricter admission and lower fanout. This preserves availability for unaffected tenants.
- Transparent Retry Slimming: at the front-door layer, observe request fingerprinting and collapse identical concurrent retry attempts within a 250ms coalescing window to a single in-flight execution where safe. Return interim progress heartbeats to callers when possible.
- Short-term KV cache compaction: limit prefix cache retention to reduce memory pressure in nodes handling amplified workloads.

Patch and rollout plan:
- PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 (server-side router + router config flags).
- Edge shim PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/991 (coalescing and lightweight fingerprinting).
- Canary rollout to eu-west-1 and us-west-2 with 1% traffic for 1 hour, then 5% for 2 hours, pending no regression. Feature flags to allow immediate rollback.
- Telemetry: add dedicated Dashboards and Alerts (hosted-stream-coalesce, fallthrough-rate) before canary.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and coalescing semantics added.
- Integration tests that simulate concurrent retry storms (100 clients, jitter) added to CI.
- Staging soak where synthetic tenant surge is replayed for 4 hours.

Customer communication and escalation handling:
- Drafted customer-facing status note with SRE & Support: Confluence link in links below.
- For critical customers impacted, support will enable per-tenant fastpath to isolate them from the amplified pool while rollout proceeds.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Coalescing window size (250ms chosen after load testing; too long harms latency-sensitive clients).
- Whether to introduce idempotency tokens at SDK layer: long-term solution but out-of-scope for immediate patch.
- Transparent coalescing may slightly change emitted traces — added headers to preserve trace continuity.

Follow-up (post-resolution) work planned:
- Rework streaming deserialization to avoid buffer retention on aborted/replayed chunks.
- Per-tenant adaptive hysteresis with burst allowance counters.
- SDK guidance + default backoff policy changes to minimize naive retry storms.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary shows p50 and p95 token generation latency improvement for affected tenants by >=30% vs pre-patch under synthetic retries.
- No increase in error rates for control tenants.
- Support runbook updated and customers with active escalations have been contacted and offer of isolation accepted where requested.
